_comment: The agent harness configuration. ONE file, two readers (config.ps1 for the
scripts, config.py for the Mattermost bridge), so a value is never defined
twice in two languages. Precedence, resolved only in the loaders:
built-in defaults < this file < harness.local.json (gitignored) < environment
This file is committed and MUST NOT contain secrets - it holds policy and
topology only. Machine-specific or experimental overrides go in
harness.local.json beside it.

extension._why_locked: operator 2026-08-28: the surface the operator drives interactively must never silently degrade to a weaker model.

mattermost._note: switchable in a thread with 'profile: <name>', the same shape as the existing 'model:' and 'worktree:' directives.

claude-code._note: a Claude Code agent - a subagent in an editor session, or 'claude -p' spawned by the bridge. Model names are CLI aliases, not API ids.

_why_container_workspace: The daemon's workspace root INSIDE the container (little-coder.config.yaml's
workspace.path), which is also the agent's cwd for every task. The quadrant
comparison mirrors a run workspace into this directory and mirrors the changed
files back out, because little-coder's workspace is a docker VOLUME shared with
open-terminal - there is no bind mount from a host worktree into the container, and
the daemon's own focus path clones from a git-host URL only (urlnorm.py rejects
local paths and file://). Declared here rather than assumed in code so a config
change is the whole change if the daemon's workspace ever moves.
little-coder._note: the local substrate: little-coder reaches llama-cpp through LiteLLM. Dispatched by dispatch.ps1 (Invoke-HarnessTask).
_why_lease: Focusing this runner WIPES its workspace and a task runs arbitrary commands in it,
so a dispatch is a live-plane mutation. dispatch.ps1's Assert-RunnerLease refuses
unless the named lease is held BY THE CALLER (lease.ps1 -Acquire -Name coder).
A runner without this key needs no lease - the policy lives here, not in the code.
Added 2026-08-30: the code claimed 'callers take the coder lease' in a comment while
nothing acquired, asserted or checked one.
_why_docker_exec: This runner declared endpoint 'http://127.0.0.1:8090' until 2026-08-30. That door did
so `curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/health` from the host is connection-refused while
`docker exec little-coder curl http://localhost:8090/health` answers. Nothing called
it, so nothing noticed. base_url is therefore CONTAINER-LOCAL and only meaningful
DECLARES, not publishes: not even 9091 exists on the running container - `docker port`
prints nothing and .NetworkSettings.Ports is {"9090/tcp":[]}. That disagreement is
measured; its CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. See MODULE.md's DECLARED-is-not-EXISTS note.
The port stays unpublished deliberately: daemon.py's own header says 'It is NOT the
task-trigger authentication surface; that is lc-mcpo', and lc-mcpo was retired
2026-08-20 - so POST /tasks (arbitrary agent execution) and POST /admin/shutdown are
unauthenticated. Reaching them through `docker exec` needs Docker access, which is
already an admin-equivalent boundary; publishing them on the host loopback would hand
them to every process on the machine for no capability the harness needs.
REVERT: set transport to 'http', base_url to 'http://127.0.0.1:8090', and add
dispatch.ps1's Invoke-LcApi already implements the http transport.

fixture._note: scaffolding for the quadrant comparison's own proof: performs an item deterministically with no model at all. status 'self-test' is load-bearing - quadrant/schema.json's comparable_runner_statuses excludes it, so it can never appear in a decision table, and test_quadrant.py asserts no profile assigns a role to it.

_comment: The TARGET axis (PLAN 1 L3), orthogonal to the runner axis and living in
configuration rather than code: 'Nothing in the pipeline layer knows which
quadrant it is in.'

self._note: the org works on THE REPOSITORY IT IS POINTED AT - a worktree off that repo's ref, plane leases for shared runtime, that repo's branch policy. Which repository is the VENUE's question, not this target's: in a gym run 'self' is a worktree of the arena, and in a workspace-venue smoke run it is ai-stack. The quadrant harness uses a DETACHED worktree so a comparison never leaves a branch behind.

project._note: the org pointed at an external project: agent-org's clone/workspace model, git-proxy containment, the GitHub App as the door. For a COMPARISON the workspace is a local disposable repo - a comparison must never be the first thing to touch a real target.

_comment: The runner x target comparison. PLAN 2's U4 column, QUOTED IN FULL because the
first word is the one this config used to drop:
"Gym: same anchored item run per quadrant (runner x target), outcomes
compared; stall -> oracle observed firing at least once"
'Gym:' is bound four lines above that table: "'gym' means measured runs in
`ai-orchestration-gym`, never live planes or a real target." The restatement
here previously began at 'same anchored item', so the one clause naming the
VENUE was the one clause missing from the config's own copy of the
requirement - and a four-cell comparison was then run against ai-stack and
read as satisfying the column. `venue` below is that clause, as data.
Listing the axes here rather than in code is what lets a fifth runner or a
third target be a config edit; the harness derives the matrix, and its report
always renders one row per configured cell whether or not that cell produced
a record.

_why: THE ARENA. The gym's own README: `main` is the arena holding the training
project the org iterates on, force-swapped per scenario and never built on
by hand; the harness branch holds the scenario catalog and the run ledger.
So `ref` is `main` - a run against the harness branch would be working on
the gym's tooling, not in its arena.
The path is RELATIVE and is resolved against the MAIN CHECKOUT of this repo
(the git common dir's parent), not against the caller's worktree: harness
sessions run in .claude/worktrees/wt-<id>, where '..' means something else
entirely. Override per machine with $AI_STACK_GYM_REPO or --repo.
quadrant/venue.py REFUSES this venue if it resolves to this repository.
ai-stack itself - the venue a smoke run of the HARNESS uses. It does NOT
satisfy any 'Gym:' column and quadrant/schema.json says so in the venue
kind's own rules, so selecting it cannot quietly produce evidence for U4.

quadrant._repeats_note: 1 means every cell is n=1 and the report says so in those words. Raise it to 2+ before treating any difference between quadrants as real.
quadrant._results_dir_note: NOT under .claude/. Measured 2026-08-30: a claude-code run whose workspace lived at .claude/quadrant-runs/.../workspace had every Write and Edit turned into a permission request - Claude Code treats .claude/ as a sensitive path - so the quadrant scored 1/2 on a task the model had already solved correctly in its reply. The harness would have been measuring its own directory choice.

all-cloud._desc: the default everywhere; all three roles on cloud opus

all-local._desc: no cloud calls at all; needs the inference plane healthy

local-work-cloud-review._desc: cheap production, expensive judgement - the reviewer is the last gate before a merge

cloud-work-local-test._desc: expensive production, cheap verification - useful when the test plan is mechanical

pipeline._note: the role -> state -> duty table stays in queue.ps1: it is behavior, not tuning. Turning a gate off here is an operator decision with a real cost, which is why both are listed explicitly rather than assumed.

_env_files_note: Runtime files a worktree needs but git will not materialize. The two recipe
.env files live INSIDE the OB1 submodule, so a fresh worktree clone never has
them and `docker compose -f OB1/docker/docker-compose.yml config` fails there
while passing in the main checkout - which is how the offline harness came to
fail only in worktrees. An ARRAY of lines, like _comment above: a JSON string
cannot contain a raw newline, and the first version of this note did. PowerShell
ConvertFrom-Json accepted it; Python json.loads did not - and this file has BOTH
readers (config.ps1 and config.py), so it would have broken the bridge alone.
